questions.question:
Three coins are tossed. Consider the events:
A: 'three heads or three tails'
B: 'at least two heads'
C: 'at most two heads'
Of the pairs (A,B), (A,C) and (B,C), which are independent? Which are mutually exclusive?
solutionSteps: $C = \{TTT, TTH, THT, HTT, THH, HTH, HHT\}, P(C)=7/8$.
$B \cap C = \{HHT, HTH, THH\}, P(B \cap C) = 3/8$. Not mutually exclusive.
Only (A,B) are independent. None are mutually exclusive (intersections are non-empty).

questions.question:
Case Study: In a relay race, there are 5 teams A, B, C, D, E.
(i) What is the probability that A, B, C finish first, second and third respectively?
(ii) What is the probability that A, B, C are the first three to finish (in any order)?
(iii) What is the probability that A finishes before B?
solutionSteps: (i) A-B-C-X-Y. X,Y can be D,E or E,D (2 ways). Prob = $2/120 = 1/60$.
(ii) First 3 are {A,B,C}. They can be arranged in $3! = 6$ ways. Remaining 2 in $2!$ ways. Total favorable = $6 \times 2 = 12$. Prob = $12/120 = 1/10$.
(iii) By symmetry, in half the cases A is before B. Prob = $1/2$.
